audit_scope.description: This audit covers EL P2P networking changes (eth/69 protocol from EIP-7642), CL P2P changes (PeerDAS data column gossip/req-resp/publishing from Fulu specs), and the EL-CL trust boundary via engine_getBlobsV2. EIP-7910 (eth_config JSON-RPC) is out of scope per bug bounty rules.

in_scope: P2P Network (eth/69 handshake, history sync, receipt transfer)
out_of_scope: JSON-RPC API (eth_config - explicitly out of scope per bug bounty)

in_scope: P2P Network (PeerDAS data column gossip validation, req/resp protocols)

engine_api.description: EL-CL communication via Engine API is authenticated using JWT and considered semi-trusted
engine_api.rationale: Co-located EL and CL clients communicate via authenticated Engine API (JWT). The Engine API is considered a trusted boundary, but data returned by EL may not be fully verified by CL in all cases (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 is used without KZG verification). If the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data may be propagated to the network.
security_implications: Engine API is authenticated via JWT
Some data from EL may be used without full verification by CL
Compromised EL can affect CL behavior
engine_api.note: Vulnerabilities in Engine API implementation are in-scope, but attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity

Critical.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Exploit an EIP/specification or client bug to easily create an infinite amount of ETH which is finalized by the network
Take down the entire network by sending a single malicious on-chain transaction that ends up crashing all clients
Critical.impact: Entire network (>50% validators or all clients)
Critical.attack_vector: Single malicious on-chain transaction or network packet

High.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 33% of the network
Bring down more than 33% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
High.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Medium.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 5% of the network
Bring down more than 5% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Medium.impact: More than 5% of the network (or >1% of validators for slashing)
Medium.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Low.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting at least 0.01% of the network
Bring down more than 0.01% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Low.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Submit malformed transactions, abuse eth_config for reconnaissance. NOTE: JSON-RPC is OUT OF SCOPE per bug bounty.

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Send invalid data column sidecars to bypass validation pipeline, equivocation attacks, resource exhaustion via unverifiable proposer sidecars queued for later processing
Request data outside serve range, send malformed requests to exhaust resources
Advertise false custody_group_count in ENR, fake fork digest/nfd fields, eclipse via custody group manipulation
Return corrupted blob data that CL converts to invalid data columns and propagates without KZG verification (trust boundary violation)

Local validator set is under operator control (SEMI_TRUSTED). Configuration issues requiring operator error are out-of-scope per trust assumptions. However, the supernode threshold check is relevant to network-level custody obligations so boundary edge is still modeled.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/69 P2P Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/69 protocol (Status handshake, BlockRangeUpdate, GetReceipts/Receipts)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary eth/69 protocol messages. All handshake fields (networkid, genesis, forkid, earliestBlock, latestBlock), BlockRangeUpdate messages, and receipt data must be fully validated. Peers may lie about available history ranges or send malformed receipts.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossip Peer via PeerDAS Data Column Subnets
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P gossip peers are unauthenticated. Any node can publish data column sidecars on gossip subnets. The CL runs a 13-step validation pipeline (structural validity, subnet routing, slot timeliness, finalization check, proposer signature, parent checks, finalized ancestry, inclusion proof, KZG proofs, anti-equivocation, proposer index). All data must pass every check before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Requesting Peer via PeerDAS Req/Resp Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers requesting data column sidecars are unauthenticated. Requests must be validated against the data_column_serve_range and MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS limits. Responses must only include sidecars that pass gossip validation. Malicious peers may request data outside serve range to probe node state or exhaust resources.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer via discv5 Discovery Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: discv5 ENR records (eth2 fork digest, cgc, nfd fields)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Discovery network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can advertise arbitrary ENR records with false custody_group_count (cgc) or fork digest values. ENR fields must be validated: fork compatibility checked, custody_group_count verified against CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, and ongoing custody compliance scored.

trusted_external_entities.name: Local Execution Layer via Engine API (engine_getBlobsV2)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Co-located EL communicates via JWT-authenticated Engine API. CL explicitly skips KZG verification for locally-retrieved blobs from engine_getBlobsV2. This is a critical trust boundary: if the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted blobs are converted to invalid data columns and propagated to the network without verification. The anti-equivocation cache must also cover locally-imported columns.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossip Network (Beacon Block/Data Column Trigger)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Valid beacon blocks or data column sidecars received via gossip trigger the local EL blob query (engine_getBlobsV2). The gossip data itself is validated before triggering the query, but this creates a chain: untrusted gossip → semi-trusted EL query → unverified blob data → propagated data columns.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All Status message fields (version, networkid, genesis, forkid, earliestBlock, latestBlock, latestBlockHash) must be validated. networkid, genesis, and forkid must match local chain. Incompatible peers must be disconnected. Peers may claim false earliestBlock/latestBlock ranges.

BlockRangeUpdate messages must be rate-limited (max once per epoch / 32 blocks). Peers claiming false block ranges must be penalized via peer scoring when they fail to serve claimed blocks. No implicit trust in peer-reported history ranges.

Receipts received in new eth/69 format (without bloom filters) must be decoded and validated. Bloom filters must be recomputed locally from logs if needed. Receipt data must be verified against expected block hashes. Malformed receipt encoding must be rejected.

Full 13-step validation pipeline must be applied: (1) structural validity via verify_data_column_sidecar, (2) correct subnet routing, (3) slot timeliness with MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY, (4) slot above finalization, (5) proposer signature verification, (6) parent block seen, (7) parent block valid, (8) slot > parent slot, (9) finalized checkpoint ancestry, (10) KZG commitments inclusion proof, (11) KZG column proofs, (12) anti-equivocation uniqueness, (13) expected proposer index. REJECT penalties propagate to peer scoring. IGNORE silently drops.

Requested range must be checked against data_column_serve_range. Requests outside serve range return ResourceUnavailable (error code 3). Response must not exceed MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS. Response ordering by (slot, column_index) must be enforced. Only sidecars passing gossip validation may be served.

Block epoch must be >= minimum_request_epoch. Requests for blocks before minimum return ResourceUnavailable (error code 3). Response must not exceed MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS. Only sidecars passing gossip validation may be served.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: discv5 ENR record parsing (eth2, cgc, nfd fields)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: ENR fields must be parsed and validated: eth2 fork digest must match expected value, cgc (custody_group_count) must be >= CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (MAY reject if insufficient), nfd (next_fork_digest) must be checked for fork compatibility. Peers MUST NOT be disconnected before fork boundary for nfd mismatch but MAY be disconnected at/after. Ongoing custody compliance must be scored.

CRITICAL TRUST BOUNDARY: CL skips KZG verification for blobs returned by engine_getBlobsV2. JWT authentication ensures only the co-located EL responds. However, if the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted blob data will be converted to invalid data columns and propagated to the gossip network. The anti-equivocation cache must correctly cover locally-imported data columns (not just gossip-received ones) to prevent equivocation via the local EL path.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: gossipsub beacon_block / data_column_sidecar topics triggering engine_getBlobsV2
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The triggering gossip message (beacon block or data column sidecar) must have passed full gossip validation before the engine_getBlobsV2 query is initiated. The kzg_commitments from the validated block are used as the query parameter. An attacker cannot trigger arbitrary EL queries without first passing gossip validation.
